title: Count Primes
statement: Return the number of prime numbers strictly less than `n`.
hints: Trial division of every integer is correct and too slow for large n.
The sieve of Eratosthenes marks multiples of each prime.
Start marking at p * p, and only consider odd primes after handling 2. The simple sieve that starts at 2 * p is enough to learn.
editorial: Create a boolean array is_prime of length n, initially true, with 0 and 1 false. For each p from 2 while p * p < n, if p is still prime, mark p*p, p*p+p, ... as composite. The answer is the number of true entries. Multiples below p*p were marked by smaller primes.
